mathematical_statement: For the frozen one-sided recursion, new complement columns at U_n to U_{n+1} lie in a fresh column half. If every newly UNSAT prefix row has empty accumulated U_n complement fibre, then the old and new complement supports have disjoint row and column projections and no old/new complement coupling. Thus reuse of an already active prefix row is necessary for backward coupling by this mechanism.
proved_instance: At U16 to U17, all eight new prefix rows were absent from the exact nonempty G16 complement row projection, so U17 is block-separable and rho(G17)<=sigma(G17)<=4.
transfer_conditions: the same frozen one-sided recursive complement construction is used
the new band is classified exactly rather than sampled
the old nonempty row projection is complete
new columns lie outside the old column projection
old and new local generator-separating families are legal in the same full-cover polarity
falsifiers: a newly UNSAT prefix row already has a nonempty old complement fibre
a new complement column lies in the old column projection
the recursive rule contributes complement edges in another quadrant
the old active-row inventory or new UNSAT classification is incomplete
non_guarantees: a row-projection collision is not sufficient for cover growth
failure of block separability is not a lower bound
the U17 finite upper bound is not a uniform recurrence
no circuit lower bound or P-versus-NP authority
no strict RAKL discovery credit because U17 was publicly exposed before candidate freeze
